abstract: In this paper an approach for a CMOS voltage reference with the ability to calibrate both voltage over temperature behavior and absolute voltage value is presented. This is achieved by electronic controlled trimming of resistances in the PTAT current source and output amplifier. For the transistors in the PTAT current source, the diode connected reference source and the error amplifier a common size of width W = 1μm and length L = 4μm was chosen. The design has a nominal total current consumption of 3.4μA and operates at a minimum supply voltage as low as 800mV for the chosen V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ref2</sub> of 700mV. The design can be optimized for even lower current consumption by using higher resistances as well as narrower and/or longer transistors. However, such an adaption increases the chip area due to the larger size of both resistors and FETs.

articleTitle: Wavelength-scaled ultra-wide bandwidth multi-function phased arrays
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: The Navy has sponsored past programs designed to demonstrate that advanced, multi-function phased arrays are a feasible concept. Based on these successes, the goal of the Integrated Topside program is to improve platform capability and flexibility while greatly reducing the proliferation of topside antennas and their associated mutual interference by combining many systems (currently performed by separate antennas) into a smaller set of wideband phased-array apertures. Assuming performance metrics can be met, the limiting factor becomes cost. For satellite communications, a relatively large aperture is required to achieve a narrow beam width. Further, the element spacing of the array is dictated by the highest frequency of operation, with the overall size of the array typically dictated by the aperture requirements at the lowest frequency. This combination a large aperture for low frequencies with dense element spacing for high frequencies results in excessive element counts leading to prohibitive costs. While the cost factor is somewhat offset by the fact that several systems can be combined into a single system, in many cases the antennas being retired are relatively inexpensive reflector-based systems. However, because of the great potential benefits in driving down the number of onboard antennas and improving system flexibility, the Navy has considerable interest in reducing the cost of wideband phased-array systems.

articleTitle: Wideband tunable stubs using phase shifters
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: A novel technique to realize a tunable λ/2 stub is presented. The technique can be applied in the realization of tunable filters with stubs. The effective length of the stub is made tunable by replacing part or whole of the line by a phase shifter. This technique can overcome limitations of tunable stubs using varactor diodes such as the limited C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</sub>/C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">min</sub> ratio of varactors which in turn limits the tuning range. In addition, in filter applications it is possible to decrease the size of a filter by using a phase shifter instead of several varactor diodes in series or in parallel. The amplitude response of the tunable stub is a function of the slope of the insertion phase of the phase shifter. If the insertion phase is a linear function of frequency, a tunable transmission line is mimicked best. The technique is demonstrated using the commercially available PS094-315 phase shifter from Skyworks and a tuning range of 35% is achieved. The tunable shunt stub can be further enhanced by introducing a transmission zero in the second passband using a transmission line and a varactor. The fabricated enhanced shunt stub has a tuning range of more than 35%. In addition, phase shifter with a larger bandwidth can increase the tuning range further. This can be realized for example with switched binary phase shifter. The phase shifter used here was not specifically designed for application in tunable stubs and it is anticipated that custom designed phase shifters can improve the performance substantially.

articleTitle: RF performance of lightweight multi horn switched beam antennas made of injection molded plastics for unmanned systems
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: The high data rates and sophisticated networking waveforms used in unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) often require a high-gain agile beam antenna subsystem to meet throughput requirements. An antenna subsystem with the required capabilities that is compatible with the size, weight, power and cost constraints of a UAV thus becomes an enabling technology for these future systems. Two approaches are available for agile electronically steered antennas: phased arrays and switched multibeam antennas (SB As). The high cost of phased arrays is difficult to reconcile with lightweight UAVs. The overall cost of a phased array or an SBA depends on the number of elements used and the relative cost of the elements. In general, SBAs tend to cost less than phased arrays because a switch is less expensive than a phase shifter or T/R module. Furthermore, emerging technologies such as injection molded plastics are available for additional SBA weight and cost reductions. This paper discusses the path to a lightweight, low cost SBA capable of implementation on very small UAVs. This is a continuation of the work previously presented at the 2007 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium [1]. In 2007, the study of lightweight SBAs utilizing injection molded plastics was at an early stage; the only available results were simulations of subcomponents of the SBA. In the subsequent years, EMS has completed the design, manufacture, and RF performance tests of an integrated SBA assembly utilizing injection molded plastics for cost and mass savings.

articleTitle: Study of microwave Dielectric Resonator Oscillator long term frequency stability
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: Based on the frequency degradation information represented by internal state transition, this paper presents a degradation modeling framework and uses it to study the Dielectric Resonator Oscillator (DRO) long term frequency stability. Analysis of the factors influencing DRO frequency revealed that stress release in the microwave dielectric maybe play an important role in performance degradation of DRO. Then frequency degradation models are created and fitted by the degradation data coming from the Accelerated Degradation Test (ADT). The result indicates that the model significantly reflects the DRO practical degradation process with an impressively small sum of residuals.

articleTitle: A new SLM OFDM scheme with low complexity for PAPR reduction in CR system
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: The ever growing demand for wireless services has placed enormous burden on valuable resources such as spectral bandwidth. Cognitive Radio (CR) with dynamic access is becoming the main trend of the next generation wireless communication system as it can greatly increase the efficiency of spectrum utilization. OFDM, which can allocate spectrum resource conveniently, is the main modulation scheme of CR. Recently, OFDMA has been adopted by IEEE802.22 Wireless Regional Area Network (WRAN) as the transmission technique of physics layer and multi-address access technique. However, high peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR) of signal is a major problem of OFDM system. High peak value would result in distortion of signals for the non-linearity of power amplifier, which would create interference to licensed users.

articleTitle: Miniaturization challenges for autonomously phased arrays in a CubeSat application
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: This paper described the miniaturization challenges in implementing an RDA architecture for a heavily resource-constrained CubeSat platform; by demonstrating this, a transition towards implementation on other highly mobile platforms can be accelerated. Addressing size, weight, and power in RDAs can be achieved through downsizing of circuitry through PCB design while reducing power consumption in each of the operating states, most importantly the prevalent static state.

articleTitle: Simulation of shipborne small HF antennas with RWG discretization and fast solver
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: In this paper, an alternative approach has been used to analyze an electrically small antenna (1.2m in the 2-30 MHz band) in a large ship (238m length) using a generic EFIE simulation code with Rao, Wilton and Glisson (RWG) basis functions, with the minimum necessary modifications to tackle the lowfrequency and multiscale issues that lead to a very poorly conditioned linear system.

articleTitle: Azimuth pattern design to reduce interference in overlapping sectors using combined tilt
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: This paper focused on the effects of the combined tilt to decrease the interference from overlapping sectors in urban areas. The simulation results showed that the characteristics when using a combination of mechanical up-tilt and electrical down-tilt can narrow the azimuth beam patterns. We found that the larger the mechanical up-tilt and number of elements were, the narrower the azimuth beam patterns became. The conditions to avoid a loss in gain due to the grating lobes were shown. The application of the combined tilt to shaped beams that have very sharp curve characteristics was examined. The influence of shaped beams on the coverage areas was investigated, and the effects of decreasing the interference from overlapping sectors and increasing the SIR were shown.

articleTitle: Use of wireless sensor network on CS/CE curriculum
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: Wireless sensor network (WSN) has been a hot research topic and widely deployed in many settings that require data acquisition, processing and communication on sensor devices equipped with a simple low powered microcontroller. This computing paradigm on long lasting operations of battery powered devices is resulted from state-of-the-art research efforts of computer science (CS) and computer engineering (CE) disciplines. This technology covers a variety of core CS and CE concepts ranging from computer architecture, operating systems, computer network, embedded systems, to software engineering. Its low cost and highly portable natures serve as a high cost effective learning lab platform for CS/CE undergraduate curricula.

articleTitle: 3D FDTD modeling of a clinical system for microwave imaging
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: There is a need for novel breast cancer detection systems to overcome the limitations with today's modalities. Microwave based system has the potential to become both sensitive and specific in this application. We have studied and evaluated a possible design for a clinical system as well as developed an accurate image reconstruction algorithm to work with this system.

articleTitle: Multi-band CDMA/GPS embedded antenna for USB applications
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: In this paper we present the design of a broadband monopole antenna suitable for multi-band wireless applications in the form factor of USB dongle. By utilizing the PCB layers and the device chassis as the main radiating element, we successfully demonstrate that it is possible to seamlessly merge the antenna into the chassis and excite the monopole mode of chassis by a reciprocal feed fashion. The designed antenna proves to have advantages of high efficiency, good radiation pattern as well as low cost for production. We are also investigating the possibility of replacing the matching circuit by a LTCC module to further reduce the size of the antenna.

articleTitle: Approximation of creeping waves of circular PEC cylinders in shadow region
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: It can be concluded that several wedges are needed to provide adequate accuracy of the field strength in shadow region compared with the Keller's method. It is not clear yet how to determine the number of wedges based on the cylinder sizes, frequencies, range of the observer, and other factors, to assure simulation accuracy.

articleTitle: Application of a high frequency Ultra-Wide-Band waveform to the Small Marine User
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: A high frequency UWB waveform has been investigated, including application to surface wave propagation over seawater. A calculation based upon anticipated noise (approximately galactic for non-populated locations) and the computed electric field at one mile range indicates that a 13 dB signal to noise ratio is available at 31 miles. Assuming that the minimum time between pulses is equal to a pulse width, or 800 ns, the maximum data rate would be 1.25 Mbits/sec, enabling significant data transfer for the short transmit times anticipated with multiple small users.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic interferences caused by the common-mode noises from stacked I/O connectors and their treatments
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: The electromagnetic interferences (EMI) caused by noises resulted from the common mode of stacked I/O connectors are analyzed using both numerical simulations and experimental measurements. A strategy is presented to suppress the noise level and its emission as well, which is found to be very effective as shown in our examination.

articleTitle: Blind cognitive-MAC: A Bayesian game theoretic perspective
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: The proposed blind cognitive-MAC (BC-MAC) protocol highlights a practical approach for the cognitive system designer. Using the Bayesian game theoretic approach coupled with the proposed Bayesian learing/ reasoning (BLA) for the self-awareness of the secondary users (SUs), the cognitive radios can always learn the actually changing curve of the cognitive environment. This will help the SUs to make the right selection of the transmission strategy. We conclude that the Bayesian equilibrium solutions for the BC-MAC protocol exist under some minor conditions, and the presented BLA can rationally learn the context after a few conflicts and collisions. Numerical results verify these consecutions and show that the performance can be improved a lot measured by signal-to-interference.

articleTitle: Cross-layer performance analysis in cooperative relay networks with poission and self-similar traffic input
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: In this paper, by many simulation measurements, we analyze and compare fully effects on network performance with Poisson traffic input of traditional SRD traffic flows and FBM traffic input of LRD traffic flows, in terms of tail distribution and packet loss probability of the queue length under the condition of infinite and finite buffer cache by adopting direct transmission (DT), amplify-and-forward (AF) and decode-and-forward (DF) transmissions for infrastructure based twohop relay wireless networks.

articleTitle: On the development of a low-cost real-time remote patient monitoring system using a novel non-invasive microwave vital signs sensor
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: In this paper we describe the telemedicine related research and development efforts at Hawaii Center for Advanced Communications (HCAC). Our group has prototyped an interactive telemedicine system comprising of several medical sensors for remote diagnosis, and has design a novel non-invasive microwave vital signs sensor and associated digital signal processing (DSP) methods for continuous remote monitoring applications. The microwave sensor measures an integrated signal that when processed provides heart rate, respiration rate, changes in lung-fluid content, as well as the stroke volume. The developed low cost interactive telemedicine prototype, the design and measurements of the microwave sensor, as well as the signal analysis technique used to extract vital signs are described in the paper.

articleTitle: Uplink ad hoc cooperation by distributed equalization under a constrained backhaul
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: Theoretical analysis of base station cooperation methods have proven their potential for solving interference limitation in today's cellular networks by showing immense capacity and fairness gains. However, a major downside of base station cooperation is the additional information exchanged amongst base stations which has been the motivation for recent work on backhaul efficient cooperation schemes. In this paper, we introduce a method that is based on distributed equalization and joint decoding, which has several benefits when compared to other kinds of distributed antenna systems. On the one hand, no additional exchange of channel information is required and on the other, distributed equalization provides an elegant solution for backhaul efficient cooperation with outdated channel knowledge at the scheduler.

articleTitle: An experimental evaluation of antenna array calibration to compensate the mutual coupling effect
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: This paper shows that the calibration matrix is effective for the removing the mutual coupling effect of antenna array via numerical analysis. In measurement, the antenna pattern distortion by the stand-alone antenna element situation and the calibrated array situation is almost equal. As a future work, we have to bear out the proposed calibration system in case of more than three elements situation.

articleTitle: Wide band planar monopole antenna covered with magnetic material
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: This paper introduces the novel wide band planar monopole antenna with parasitic elements covered magnetic material to reduce the antenna size for wireless communication. The VSWR less than 2 was obtained from 1.84-13.67 GHz and the band width was 152% in the simulation results. The miniaturization of the magnetically-loaded planar monopole antenna has been investigated and the antenna area was reduced about 65%. So, the proposed antenna was useful for mobile and wireless equipments. The effects of the magnetic material and this amount depend on the arranging position. The VSWR and radiation patterns must be confirmed in the experiment.

articleTitle: Medical monitoring and diagnostics using ingestible capsule antennas: An exciting paradigm in bio-telemetry
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: Technological advancement over the past decade has enabled the use of smart capsules (electronic digestible pills) in biomedical applications. These systems help in the treatment and diagnosis of various diseases (GI tract diseases). This paper presents ingestible capsule antenna designs for smart pill systems suitable for medical monitoring and diagnostic applications in the exciting field of bio-telemetry. Firstly, an RFID bio-capsule tag is proposed for medicine monitoring purposes. The design of the tag is based on concept of inductive feed loop coupled to conformal meandered dipole. The tag performance is evaluated inside the human body in terms of impedance, radiation pattern and power reflection characteristics. The unique tag design matches to the chip impedance only when the tag is inside the human body. In the second part, a novel conformal planar offset meandered dipole capsule antenna is proposed for medical diagnostic procedures. The antenna performance is evaluated by studying the impedance, radiation, polarization and return loss characteristics inside the human body model. A link budget is evaluated to ensure successful and robust wireless telemetry.

articleTitle: Linear combination based energy detection algorithm under low SNR for cognitive radios
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: The LC algorithm is proposed to detect PU signal, especially under low SNR. We describe the LC algorithm, and derive the optimal decision threshold for the proposed LC algorithm. Simulation results show that the LC based spectrum sensing algorithm always outperforms the two conventional criteria. Compared with the CFAR criterion and the CDR criterion, the LC algorithm has more than 8dB gain in SNR.

articleTitle: Paradigm of future wireless networks with multi-domaill collaboration
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: In this talk, a service-driven architecture of wireless network is proposed to incorporate with MDC. Tliis architecture reveals the fundamental principle of MDC that multi-domain is used to create the degree of freedom (DOF), while multi-domain collaboration is to effectively exploit the benefit of the DOF. Moreover, a glimpse of promising ways to increase the transmission capacity of wireless networks with collaboration among power, space, and frequency domains is given. Likewise, a novel framework supporting aggregate broadcasting is contrived to significantly improve system capacity by utilizing the similarity of content in time, space, and inherent delay tolerance. In the end of this talk, the representative related research programs hi China, such as National basic research program (973) and National High-tech research program (863), are briefly introduced.

articleTitle: Systems delay characteristics of a busy-tone protocol in CCA modified, long range IEEE 802.11 networks
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: This paper discusses the delay characteristics and packet drop ratio performance of Busy Tone Multiple Access Protocol (BTMAP) for distances up to 48Km in IEEE 802.11 networks. The impact of the Contention Window (CW) is discussed. We note that a larger CW will increase the mean packet delay but decrease the packet drop ratio. Long range also significantly degrades the delay and packet drop ratio performance of the BTMAP, however, with the same number of users, a larger cell will cause higher drop ratio but shorter delay. This indicates that larger distances increasingly corrupt packets and are problematic to long range communications. At extremely long range (48Km), by choosing a user number less than CW, it is still possible to control the mean packet delay to under 100ms which is acceptable for VoIP networks, but the packet drop ratio is remains high due to transmission delay.

articleTitle: A study on applying nonlinear models for spectrum shape estimation
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: In this study, it is investigated the validity of applying nonlinear device model to estimate distorted spectrum shapes of the OFDM signals for spectrum sharing studies. We used an LNA and two LNBs, which are off-the-shelf devices and the spectrum shape of OFDM signal distorted by the nonlinear devices, are evaluated by the means of model-based estimation and indoor experiment. As the results, the spectrum shapes obtained by the two evaluation show good agreement, thus the model-based estimation is considered to be an effective method on the spectrum sharing studies.

articleTitle: Low-loss millimeter-wave passives on Si
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: We propose a glass platform integrating passives for the millimeter-wave module, which is fabricated by the same technology applied to Wafer-Level Packaging(WLP). The WLP is one of the confirmed IC packaging processes having merits of low cost and small package size.

articleTitle: A new relaying scheme for the MIMO relay network
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) emerged recently as a strong candidate for 4G technology in that it can exploit spatial diversity and multiplexing for increasing the system capacity without extra cost of bandwidth and power. Cooperative relaying, as an efficient solution for ubiquitous coverage, has the potential to become a key technology for future wireless communication system. The combination of MIMO and cooperative relaying technology would provide an excellent information service with high data rate and ubiquitous coverage. The MIMO relay network, with multiple relay nodes and the amplify-and-forward relaying strategy, is focused in this paper. However, the performance of the MIMO relay network is heavily dependent on the signal relaying scheme adopted by relay nodes.

articleTitle: Non-continuous SD-method for NC-OSDM transmission in cognitive radio systems
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: Suehiro's DFT (SD)-method has been proposed for multi-carrier system, which achieves higher spectrum efficiency of information transmission. In this paper, non-continuous SD-method is generated for non-continuous multi-carrier system. In Cognitive Radio (CR) systems, Non Continuous-Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplex (NC-OFDM) is employed to avoid interference for spectrum holes. This mechanism is quite suitable to involve non-continuous SD-method and formulate the Non-Contiguous Orthogonal Signal Division Multiplex (NC-OSDM) system. Simulation results show that NC-OSDM enjoys higher spectrum efficiency compared with the traditional NC-OFDM, which confirms the high efficiency in broadband CR systems.

articleTitle: Voronoi-based coverage optimization for multi-femtocells
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: Suppose a rectangle place with 9 femtocells denoted by “+”, and the femtocells are deployed previously. After conducting voronoi diagram construction, the two-object optimization problem is solved. Set the size of the rectangle place as 30×30m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, and W = [w<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i=1…9</inf> = 0.5]<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1×9</inf>. Fig 2.3 is the optimized result. Compared with Fig 2.1, which is the result with maximum radius, the overlap area is reduced, which can reduce the interference among femtocells, besides, the interference between femtocells and macrocell is also reduced because there's less radio coverage area reaching out of the rectangle place in Fig 2.3. Compared with Fig 2.2, which is the result with minimum radius, the nunlap area is visibly reduced, thus the network capacity is correspondingly improved. Based on the optimal r, the minimum transmitting power of each base station can be acquired by the formula E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i,T,min</inf> = r<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</inf><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">α</sup> E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i,R,min</inf>, i = 1, 2, …, M.

articleTitle: A novel communication service modeling
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: With forward to TCP/IP-based information network development, a large number of innovative communication services quickly emerged. In these data-based communications services, they require different communication rate and variable quality of service. And, the TCP/IP-based network's best-effort feature and statistical multiplexing strategy further makes the service capacity defined in telephone network no longer apply, when it is facing the new network and new communication services. To address the above problem, this paper introduces the difference between user-understanding information and machinery-understanding information, re-defines the communication service and proposes a service modeling. We hope to provide an objective and reasonable methods to evaluate the overall performance of the network and service, and guide the strategy management of the network and service to achieve the best balance between network efficiency and user experience.

articleTitle: Evaluating the impact of wave polarization on improvised explosive device (IED) jamming
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: In this paper, the impact of the electromagnetic wave with different polarizations on IED has been researched. The numerical results based on the two ray model have been presented. The results indicate the ground has significant impact on system performance. Comparing the various polarizations, the vertical polarization has better performance.

articleTitle: Design of a broadband low-profile microstrip antenna with multi-layer substrates
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: In this paper, the authors present that the offset-FILP fed MSA which located the FILP from the center of the patch, can increase the height of the FILP and moderate the restriction of substrates thickness. The authors also show the relationship between the input impedance and the feeding geometry, and investigate the maximum bandwidth of the offset-FILP fed MSA as well as that of the original model. Finally, the authors show that the offset-FILP fed MSA can be effectively fabricated by using substrates of same thickness.

articleTitle: A development of novel hybrid antenna for UHF and X-band
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: Novel hybrid antenna for UHF and X-band was developed, and the utility was examined by the field test in this paper. The BS reception performance of novel hybrid antenna is not inferiority in a commercial antenna. It will be necessary to improve the reception probability of HD-TV to deform the radiation pattern of UHF to the omni directional pattern in the future.

articleTitle: Wireless Network Cocast: Cooperative communications with Space-Time Network coding
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: The concept of STNC is very general. Fundamentally, it involves combining information from different sources at a relay node, which gives rise to the concept of network coding, and transmitting the combined signals in dedicated time slots from various locations in a network, which makes the space-time concept. Various traditional combining techniques can be used, including CDMA-like and OFDMA-like techniques, transform-based techniques with the use of Hadamard and Vandermonde matrices, and traditional network coding. However, a major distinction is that the combining of symbols from different sources happens inside a transmitter instead of through the air. Below is an overview of the developed STNCs.

articleTitle: Non data-aided phase estimation of 2CPM signals
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: This paper presents a novel NDA algorithm for phase estimation of 2CPM based on LD. Different with other phase synchronization methods, this estimation algorithm is completely independent of the demodulation, which means its accuracy is irrelevant to the performance of demodulation, and meanwhile its performance is relatively good. Besides, because only the first AMP component is explored, its complexity should be low.

articleTitle: Semi-automated Rotman lens design focusing on anti-jam performance
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: In this paper, the authors introduce the need for semi-automating the design of Rotman lenses and describe steps taken at SPAWAR Systems Center Pacific (SSC-PAC) to address this need. With this semi-automated design tool, the authors have been able to design several different lenses and not only verify their individual performance but compare key traits such as phase/magnitude error and insertion loss amongst all the lenses and against some lenses reported in the literature. These traits are important in improving antijam/interference performance of a Rotman lens-based wireless communications system.

articleTitle: Novel miniaturized PIFA with interdigital coupling feed for multitband operation
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: A small size PIFA using intergidital coupling feed for internal mobile phone antenna application has been proposed and studied. The proposed PIFA is easily printed on the no-ground portion of the system circuit board of the mobile phone at lowcost and occupies a very small area of 400 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> only, owing to the successful excitation of the mode as the fundamental resonant mode. The interdigital coupling feed greatly decreases the very large input impedance seen at the λ/4 mode for the traditional PIFA. The PIFA generates two wide operating bands at about 900 and 2100 MHz to cover GSM850/900 and GSM1800/1900/UMTS/WLAN operations, respectively. Good impedance matching of the two wide operating bands is achieved by using the interdigital coupling feed in the proposed PIFA.

articleTitle: Relative-localization identification of random distributed wireless sensor network nodes
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: Localization services are one of the most important services provided by wireless sensor networks. In this paper, a relative-localization identification of random deployed non-anchored nodes will be presented. Based on relative RSSI information, the system can identify which sensor nodes are placed in locations planned on map. The method can let user put any nodes anywhere (random distributed), and the nodes will locate themselves without knowing the coordinate (absolute or relative) beforehand. The algorithm and experimental verification of this method will all be detailed in this paper.

articleTitle: Compact dual-mode interdigital-loop resonator and filter application
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: A novel compact dual-mode resonator is proposed. This proposed dual-mode resonator was composed of the following features: the series capacitance is inserted for miniaturization and it's effect was also analyzed, and open stub was applied on symmetric plan for dual-mode behavior. Using this dual-mode resonator, dual-band bandpass filter of 0.2 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf> by 0.28 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf> (at odd mode resonance) for WLAN application was designed and fabricated providing an excellent verification on the attractive features of the filter, such as compact size and extra transmission zeros without increase order of filter.

articleTitle: A microcontroller configured active analog phase shifter at 1.96GHz
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: Personal Communications Service (PCS) is one of the most popular digital mobile phone services standards in North America. Its downlink frequency band is centered at 1.96GHz with 60MHz bandwidth. This research presents a microcontroller configured active analog phase shifter at 1.96GHz with phase-shifting range of 90°. The Microcontroller (MCU) increases the flexibility of control circuits and provides additional flexibility to extend the application of the phase shifter to phased array antennas. Applying algorithm to compensate the amplifier's gain-versus-control-voltage non-linear characteristics results in a small RMS phase error of 1.3° with a constant gain (|S21|>1) and increases the transmission power efficiency.

articleTitle: Advances in LC characterization with application to development of mm-wave devices
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: In this paper the current state of research in our labs on the mm-wave characterization of LCs and the application of LC in development of two devices were presented. It has been shown that the characterization of LCs can be done using the resonant and broadband methods, but each has its own advantages and disadvantages. Also shown were a LC-based reflection type phase shifter, providing a large phase shift compared to the conventional transmission line phase shifters and a long LC-based resonator with multiple tunable resonant frequencies.

articleTitle: Waveform design of FQPSK based on Bézier curve
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: FQPSK modulation with the redefined waveforms has a small envelope fluctuation, a better BER performance in AWGN channel and a not much worse power spectral efficiency than the original FQPSK. The general performance much depends on the last procedure searching for the Bezier curve control points. This new method of designing waveforms can be generalized, and a series of sets of FQPSK waveforms will be generated. Modifications can be made to the preprocessing and the regulation of control points to achive smoothness of higher order. Even some other kind of splines can be used, for example B-spline, to achieve the smoothness. These issues need more research.

articleTitle: Solution of electrically large antenna problems on scalable personal computer clusters
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: The objective of this paper is to illustrate how these problems can be best handled on scalable affordable personal computer clusters. The authors propose to achieve this goal through the use of out-of-core matrix solvers. Since, the authors do not require RAM but hard disk to deal with the storage, now the problem can be handled at an affordable personal level. Examples are presented on how this goal can be accomplished.

articleTitle: Steering Committee
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: Provides a listing of current committee members.

articleTitle: Table of contents
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: Presents the table of contents of the proceedings.

articleTitle: Reflectarray design based on interdigital gap loading element
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: In this paper, a broad angle reflectarray is designed which can scatter the normal incident wave to a large angle (up to 60°) from the normal direction of the planar reflectarray to eliminate the blind areas of the base station in wireless communication scenarios. In our research, a novel individual element which is composed of a dipole with interdigital gap structure printed on a single-layer substrate is used to construct the reflectarray. Only one degree of freedom is introduced to extend the phase range of the unit cell to more than 1000°. Furthermore, a reflectarray with a large scattering angle is designed to eliminate blind spots in communication between the base station and mobile users.

articleTitle: False peak restraint of DOA estimation using element adjustment and virtual array transformation
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: Based on the simulation outputs shown in Fig.4 (a), the conclusion can be drawn that the methods of element adjustment and virtual array transformation can be applied together to restrain the DOA estimation's false peak in the ULA with large element-spacing. One condition of the application is that the similarity between the virtual array and the real one should be as great as possible. The great similarity will reduce the transformation error, which is shown in Fig.3. The another condition of the application is that the virtual array transformation sector size must be reasonable, if the sector size is too big, DOA estimation may fail, which is demonstrated in Fig.4 (b); and if the sector size is too small, the calculation amount of DOA estimation will increase greatly.

articleTitle: Dielectric metamaterial lens antenna for wide angle beam scanning
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: The dielectric metamaterial lens antenna for wide angle beam scanning is discussed as an applicative antenna. The availability of the low-loss structure using dielectric resonator and the cause of the reduction of the antenna efficiency are clarified by the electromagnetic simulations. The validation of the design of the metamaterial lens antenna is clarified through the experiment.

articleTitle: Multiobjective optimization for RF low noise amplifier design
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: A modified semiautomatic multiobjective optimization method based on an asymptotically uniform coverage of reference set in combination with goal attainment method was proposed. The method was successfully tested on the multiobjective optimization of an RF low-noise antenna preamplifier.

articleTitle: Waveguide-to-CPW transition for an active phased array for collision avoidance radar
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: The septum-type transition couples energy with very low loss over a broad bandwidth from waveguide into a CPW circuit. This transition is virtually lossless with a bandwidth greater than 50%. It provides a single-piece, rugged, easily reproduced module that can be inexpensively produced. The multiple-septa design showed lower insertion loss over around a 4% bandwidth.

articleTitle: A 2.4 GHz fully integrated CMOS power amplifier using capacitive cross-coupling
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: The paper presented a 2.4GHz fully integrated CMOS power amplifier using capacitive cross-coupling, fabricated in 0.18µm CMOS. With a 3.3-V supply voltage, PAE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf> and PAE at 1dB compression point are 34.3% and 26.8%. P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1dB</inf>, P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sat</inf>, and PG are 25.2dBm, 27.7dBm and 26.5dB, respectively. The advantages of the proposed capacitive-cross-coupled PA are the improvement of reverse isolation and the area saving.

articleTitle: UWB antennas and channel characteristics
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: Abstract form only given. Spectrum is presently one of the most valuable goods world-wide, as the demand is permanently increasing and it can be traded only locally. Since the United States FCC has opened the spectrum from 3.1 GHz to 10.6 GHz - i.e., a bandwidth of 7.5 GHz - for unlicensed use with up to -41.25 dBm/MHz EIRP, numerous applications in communications and sensor areas are showing up. All of these applications have in common that they spread the necessary energy over a wide frequency range in this unlicensed band, in order to radiate below the limit. The results are ultra-wideband systems. These new devices exhibit quite surprising behaviors, especially at the air interface: the antenna. This talk presents insight into design, evaluation and measurement procedures for ultra-wideband (UWB) antennas, as well as into the characteristics of the UWB radio channel as a whole. UWB antenna basics and principles of wideband radiators, transient antenna characterization and UWB antenna quality measures, derived from the antenna impulse response, are topics. EM simulations and measurements of transient antenna properties in the frequency domain and in the time domain are included. Different antennas, based on different UWB principles, will be presented. Depending on the interest, there are the ridged horn antenna, Vivaldi antenna, logarithmic periodic antenna, mono-cone antenna, spiral antenna, aperturecoupled bowtie antennas, multimode antennas, sinus antenna, and impulse-radiating antennas. The channel characterization comprises ray-tracing tools for deterministic indoor UWB channel modeling and measurements. The advantages and drawbacks of UWB transmission will be discussed, depending on interest. The radiation from different antennas will be demonstrated by movies, with a pulse excitation.

articleTitle: Design considerations of 3-D single package communicator (SPC) for quad-band WCDMA/GSM cellular phone
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: A complete single package communicator (SPC) designed and implemented for 3G modem in 400 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> size and 1.3 mm height, for the first time is presented. With the help of 3-D technology, development of highly integrated active/passive components and use of latest packaging technology, the design was doable. Optimization of the RF performance of all GSM and WCDAM channels was obtainable despite the small form factor. The design was taped out.

articleTitle: Virtual array composition for iterative AOA localization sharing snapshots of coherent subarrays
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: We proposed the localization method using iterative AOA (angle of arrival) method sharing snapshots of coherent subarrays (Kawakami et al., 2009), alternative to GPS (global positioning system) that is unavailable indoor or underground. This method improves localization accuracy without increasing elements of antenna arrays, and thus the lower costs and smaller devices are expected. However, the localization accuracy of this method depends on source location, and it is not as good as expected, because we did not compose the optimal virtual array. In this paper, we research what composition shows good localization accuracy. Simulation results show that the composition based on virtual element can estimate AOA more accurately.

articleTitle: “Inkjet-printed paper/polymer-based “green” RFID and wireless sensor nodes: The final step to bridge cognitive intelligence, nanotechnology and RF?”
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: Summary form only given. In this talk, inkjet-printed flexible antennas, RF electronics and sensors fabricated on paper and other polymer (e.g.LCP) substrates are introduced as a system-level solution for ultra-low-cost mass production of UHF Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) Tags and Wireless Sensor Nodes (WSN) in an approach that could be easily extended to other microwave and wireless applications. The talk will cover examples from UHF up to the millimeter-wave frequency ranges. A compact inkjet-printed UHF “passive-RFID” antenna using the classic T-match approach and designed to match IC's complex impedance, is presented as a the first demonstrating prototype for this technology. Then, Prof. Tentzeris will briefly touch up the state-of-the-art area of fully-integrated wireless sensor modules on paper or flexible LCP and show the first ever 2D sensor integration with an RFID tag module on paper, as well as numerous 3D multilayer paper-based and LCP-based RF/microwave structures, that could potentially set the foundation for the truly convergent wireless sensor ad-hoc networks of the future with enhanced cognitive intelligence and “rugged” packaging. Prof. Tentzeris will discuss issues concerning the power sources of “near-perpetual” RF modules, including flexible minaturized batteries as well as power-scavenging approaches involving thermal, EM, vibration and solar energy forms. The final step of the presentation will involve examples from wearable (e.g. biomonitoring) antennas and RF modules, as well as the first examples of the integration of inkjet-printed nanotechnology-based (e.g.CNT) sensors on paper and organic substrates. It has to be noted that the talk will review and present challenges for inkjet-printed organic active and nonlinear devices as well as future directions in the area of environmentally-friendly (“green”) RF electronics and “smart-skin” conformal sensors.

articleTitle: Non-contiguous CI/OFDM: A new data transmission scheme for cognitive radio context
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: In this paper, the authors propose to apply non-contiguous CI/OFDM (NC-CI/OFDM) as a new data transmission scheme for CR context. Computer simulation results confirm that the proposed NCCI/OFDM system can bring desirable BER performance and low PAPR compared with the traditional NC-OFDM.

articleTitle: Armor embedded antennas for land vehicles
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: Through the army's Breakthrough Antenna Technology (BAT) Army Technology Objective - Research (ATO-R), S&TCD is pursuing to push the frontiers of antenna technology for the future warfighter. BAE Systems and the U.S. Army are developing antennas that are embedded into the armor of vehicles without impacting the armor's performance. Two main challenges drive the complexity of the design: 1. the dielectric properties of the armor material, and 2. the design of a radiating element with minimal impact to the armor structure. Measuring the dielectric properties of the armor material is necessary to employ accurate simulation models during the antenna design effort. Minimizing the impact to the armor structure is part of the larger goal of no degradation in ballistic performance of the armor due to the antenna integration.

articleTitle: Weighted localization accuracy augmentation for RSSI-based wireless sensor networks using target-to-target measurements
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: In this paper, we introduced weighted versions of two algorithms, in order to boost the accuracy for the multiple-target location estimation problem. The accuracy of the proposed algorithms was then quantitatively compared against that of the conventional algorithms using numerical simulations, which showed large accuracy improvements, particularly for large amounts of nodes. Finally, we performed an experimental validation of the proposed algorithms and showed how it is possible to reduce the RMSE of the solution in excess of 59 % when compared to that of the conventional algorithms, even with as few as 10 target nodes.

articleTitle: Broadband-interference rejection for mobile satellite communications
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: Electromagnetic interference can disrupt mobile satellite communications in both military and commercial mobile applications. Not only is this true when a high-power terrestrial source is in close proximity to a mobile satellite receiver, but it can be especially problematic when the vehicle or nearby vehicle has its own onboard interference source that overpowers the desired satellite signal. This can cause interference even if that interfering signal were out of the frequency band of the desired satellite signal, due to non-ideal filtering. To exacerbate this problem, many of these sources are ultra wideband (UWB), consisting of electromagnetic energy spread over a very large bandwidth that may overlap the desired satellite channel. In this case even the fraction of the UWB interfering power that is in-band, could potentially overpower the satellite signal power. Algorithms exist that suppress interference in narrow and broadband applications. So, rather than introduce another exotic algorithm, this paper discusses a relatively simple system for broadband interference rejection that takes advantage of the difference in bandwidths between broadband interference and a narrowband satellite signal. This is achieved by adding an interference-detection channel to the satellite receiver that adaptively steers an antenna-pattern null, in order to reject terrestrial interference caused by emitters from nearby military vehicles, as well as onboard the receiver's own vehicle.

articleTitle: Rate control and network selection for streaming services in heterogeneous networks
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: In this paper, we focus on the bandwidth allocation and reallocation scheme which uses multimode wireless access networks to guarantee the QoS of streaming services. The utility function for streaming service is proposed, which characterizes the rate adaptation and handoff delay in heterogeneous network scenario. The utility function for network provider takes into account the number of serving end users, which aims to maximize the revenue of providers. For a scalable solution about resources management in HAN, a game theory based rate control and network selection scheme(RCNS) is proposed, which is in accordance with cognition cycle. Network load estimation and prediction algorithm based on Kalman filter is introduced into bandwidth allocation game to control the overhead created by the game.

articleTitle: A smart routing scheme for wireless sensor networks
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: In this paper, we present a smart energy routing scheme for wireless sensor networks in order to improve the overall energy efficiency and the reliability in the network. Preliminary experiments have been conducted in the experiment environment and show a promising result. In the future, we will continue to improve the scheme and conduct more and longer experiments to precisely measure the benefits of our scheme.

articleTitle: Modified BOR-CROSS antenna
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: This paper presents a low-profile base station antenna, called the MBOR-CROSS, which is a modification of the BOR-CROSS developed using the design concept of the BOR-SPR. The MBOR-CROSS is composed of a conducting BOR and crossed strip plates. This MBOR-CROSS is designed for a frequency range of 470 MHz to 2625 MHz. The analysis results of the MBORCROSS are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: Performance measurement and analysis of ZRP for MANETs using network simulator-QualNet
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: Without any pre-existing fixed network infrastructure with rapid configuration of wireless connections on-the-fly, network topology in MANETs keep on changing rapidly. Thus achieving data transmissions between wireless nodes in MANETs with improved QoS parameters become a challenging issue. To achieve this one has to concentrate on the routing protocol they choose. In our paper we proposed an algorithm to provide improved quality of service via hybrid routing protocol- Zone Routing Protocol (ZRP). We have considered two reactive routing protocols Dynamic Source Routing (DSR) and Ad hoc On Demand Distance Vector (AODV) as reference for analyzing ZRP by considering route acquisition delay and quick route reconfiguration during link failure. These parameters viz., route acquisition delay and quick route reconfiguration have their impact on increase in end to end delay, this automatically decreases the number of packets received thus the throughput. We used well known network simulator QualNet version 4.5 to compare QoS parameters viz., throughput, number of bytes received, average end-to-end delay for DSR, AODV and ZRP.

articleTitle: Spectrum analysis system for Dynamic Spectrum Access policy generation
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: Discusses approaches that are expressed in coexistence policies that govern the behavior of DSA spectrum access protocol. In order to generate these policies, we are developing a Spectrum Analysis Module (SAM) that will become a key component of the policy generation system. SAM determines the relevant DSA policy parameters and prepares coexistence policies that are loaded into the DSA radios prior to their use. We expect SAM to become an integral part of operations support system necessary for deployment and use of DSA in the field.

articleTitle: Physical layer specification for wireless sensor networks dedicated to evaluation of buildings energetic performances
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: In this paper, we propose an extension of the energy model, and show the influence of the channel on energy consumption. Simulation results show that significant gains are obtained by adjusting the transmission power in function of the kind of link between the central node and individual nodes. Future works are dedicated to develop a cross-layer approach based on the presented works. Indeed, once the transmission power is adjusted, the parameters that can optimize the overall energy system are in relation to the strategies of sleep and wake up of nodes (MAC sub-layer).

articleTitle: System performance evaluation of distributed antennas based CoMP in LTE-Advanced
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: In this paper, we have summarized our analysis about distributed antennas based CoMP in LTE-Advanced and evaluated the system spectrum efficiency in three scenarios. From the results, we can see the proposed scheme achieves a higher throughput compared with centralized antennas based system. The location of antennas closed to sector center leads to the optimal system performance. With the change in the number and location of the antennas, the antennas tend to be scattered placement. The method of clustering, algorithm of antennas selection, and multi-antennas per sector, are worthy of further research.

articleTitle: Anechoic chamber evaluation using microwave optical transceiver in frequency range of 1 GHz to 18 GHz
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: We developed the optical transceiver operating up to 18 GHz and conducted the site VSWR measurement using the optical measurement system. Compared with the coaxial cable system and the optical transceiver system, the SNR of the coaxial cable system was insufficient and incapable of measuring the site VSWR above 7 GHz. On the other hand, the optical transceiver system has more than 50 dB SNR and has the capability of measuring the site VSWR in the frequency range of 1 GHz to 18 GHz. As a result, the developed optical measurement system is useful for the evaluation of the anechoic chamber for EMI up to 18 GHz.

articleTitle: Improvement of the throughput-SNR trade-off using a 4G adaptive MCM system
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: The MIMO-OFDM Adaptive MCM System changes MIMO scheme, channel coding rate, and modulation scheme, adaptively, according to the channel conditions. And the addition of Pre-coding and Antenna Subset Selection assures a better performance and higher data rate. The MIMO-OFDM Adaptive MCM System achieves a better average throughput performance than a Non Adaptive-MCM system; as SNR increases, the throughput increases almost linearly. Based on the simulation results, we conclude that the proposed MIMO-OFDM Adaptive MCM System represents a feasible solution for improving the throughput-SNR tradeoff in the next generation of mobile communication systems.

articleTitle: DOA estimation without antenna characteristics calibration for UWB signal by using sub-band processing
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: High resolution method for direction of arrival (DOA) estimation using array antenna is studied actively. In almost previous studies, it is assumed that the antenna elements have the same directional patterns. However, it is very difficult to make many antenna elements they have just the same directional patterns. Furthermore, the directional patterns are distorted due to mutual coupling between the antenna elements. The estimation accuracy is decayed if the directional patterns are distorted intensively. Generally, to avoid the effect of directional pattern distortion, antenna characteristics are calibrated before the estimation, however, it is difficult to cancel the effect of distortion when the arrival signal is very wideband because the directional patters depend on the frequency. In this paper, sub-band technique to decrease the effect of antenna pattern distortion is proposed. In the proposed scheme, received wideband signal is divided into several frequency bands and DOA is estimated in the respective frequency bands. By averaging the estimated results, the effect of antenna pattern distortion will be reduced. In the following section, configuration of proposed system is explained first. After that the effect of number of sub-band and effect of antenna characteristics on DOA estimation accuracy is discussed.

articleTitle: The 4×4 high power active integrated phased array antenna operating at 5.8 GHz for wireless information and power transmission
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: The AIPAA with high power amplifier and the heat pipe was demonstrated. The AIPAA consists of the circular patch, the high power FET, the 4-bit digital phase shifter, the DC regulator and the heat pipe cooling system. For the functions of WIPT, the power transmission with 800mW output from each array element in the 4×4 AIPAA was achieved and the BER of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup> was kept with MSK with 9 Mbps. The beam steering was also carried out within +/- 23 degrees. WIPT to the rover in the moon are expected to be one of the promising space applications.

articleTitle: Modern plastic millimeter-wave array antennas
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: This paper presents two types of millimeter-wave waveguide-type array antennas using low-loss engineering plastics not only to reduce cost but also to obtain high performances. The first one is a post-wall slotted waveguide array antenna with an offset directional beam using a post-wall rectangular waveguide inside a Grafted Olefin-Styrene resin printed circuit board. The other is a Cyclo-Olefin Polymer (COP) waveguide horn array antenna which is fabricated by injection molding process.

articleTitle: The Square Kilometre Array: Engineering opportunities
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: The Square Kilometre Array (SKA) is an international radio telescope for the 21st century which will have a total collecting area of approximately one square kilometre. Similar to present-day radio interferometers, the SKA will consist of many antennas which are spread over a large area. The signals are combined in a central computer (correlator). The resolving power is proportional to the frequency and to the largest baseline between the outermost antennas and hence it will be about ten times more sensitive than the largest single dish telescope (305 m diameter) at Arecibo (Puerto Rico), and fifty times more sensitive than the currently most powerful interferometer, the Expanded Very Large Array (EVLA, at Socorro/USA). The SKA will continuously cover most of the frequency range accessible from ground, from 70 MHz to 10 GHz (corresponding to wavelengths of 3 cm to 4 m) in the first and second phases, later to be extended to at least 25 GHz (1.2 cm). Another major improvement is the enormously wide field of view, ranging from 200 square degrees at 70 MHz to at least 1 square degree at 1.4 GHz. The speed to survey a large part of the sky, particularly at the lower frequencies, will hence be ten thousand to a million times faster than what be possible today.

articleTitle: A method to compute the packet size and to transmit the packets for the efficient VoIP communication using the MIL-STD-188-220C
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: In this paper, the authors derived the packet size and transmission protocol which guarantees high quality of data transmission as well as minimizes the initial speech transmission delay and the speech cut-off intervals caused by the packet errors. For this, the authors deducted expected time of data transmission in radiotelegraph using MIL-STD-188-220C. For VoIP communication in radio devices, it is revealed that the protocol which transmits short frames composed of 90ms sampling packets and 90ms re-transmission packets is efficient for 36kbps transmission systems, and in the systems of higher bit rates, the protocol which transmits long frames and then requests re-transmission when needed. The proper packet size and the transmission protocol which compromise multi-hop transmission for ad-hoc radiotelegraph should be developed in future work.

articleTitle: On the design of integrated HF radar systems for Homeland Security applications
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: In this paper, HCAC's research and development efforts on the development of integrated and low cost HF radar for coastal surveillance and other Homeland Security applications are summarized. The proposed design incorporates electrically small antenna for rapid deployment, supports operation on floating platforms by using enhanced DSP algorithms to mitigate clutter, incorporates improved propagation modeling to more accurately select optimum frequency channels based on atmospheric conditions and overcome the errors due to terrain effects, utilizes Genetic Programming for automatic target recognition and classification, and provides for passive radar operation utilizing existing broadcast transmitters to enable covert operation.

articleTitle: Investigation on an UWB antenna combining a caped-monopole and a dielectric resonator
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: In this paper, a hybrid antenna was presented, consisting of a dielectric ring resonator fed by a quarter wavelength monopole with an upper metal disc. This antenna was capable of achieving a bandwidth response starting from 3 GHz up to 13 GHz. Further designs will be studied to reduce the ground plane size keeping the same bandwidth that covers the whole FCC mask for UWB wireless communications. Moreover, more results will be shown later, in addition to the measured results. Such an antenna could be used in medical applications such as imaging for human body tissues.

articleTitle: A nash bargaining solution based cooperation pattern for open spectrum cognitive radio networks
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: A cooperation pattern is proposed in which cognitive users can cooperate with each other by means of relaying. The cooperation between cognitive users is modeled as a two-person bargaining problem and cooperation strategies are obtained based on Nash bargaining solution (NBS). Simulations shows that the cooperation willingness of an user depends on how appropriate its counterpart can be served as its relay.

articleTitle: A design of slotted waveguide antenna array operated at X-band
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: This paper presents a design of X-band slotted waveguide antenna array that has a linear polarization and exhibits high directivity for a long-distance communication. Especially we present a procedure that is very useful in a realistic implementation. The design is validated by numerical simulation using HFSS, and measurement results will be presented in the conference presentation.

articleTitle: The next decade of naval communications S&T - bridging the tactical divide
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: Net-centric communications implies the seamless end-to-end interconnectivity between the enterprise wide area networks and the tactical theater, both for reach-back and reach-forward capabilities. No where is this truer than for the Naval forces, with significant investment in the shore, SATCOM and afloat infrastructure. But the evolution to net-centricity is putting pressure on the tactical and subtactical communications to rise to similar bandwidth, Quality-of-Service, and applications delivery requirement, as the enterprise side. Our talk explores innovative approaches, architectures and wireless technologies to realize these warfighter networked communication goals.

articleTitle: Coverage area extention through a cooperative MAC protocol
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: While diversity is the main purpose of cooperation, additional objectives have been recently investigated. Addressing this issue of error recovery, we recently introduced a Partnership-based Cooperative MAC (PC-MAC) protocol with random partner assignment. PC-MAC is based on the DCF (Distributed Coordination Function) protocol used in the IEEE 802.11 standard. Rate adaptation schemes are used in the latter to increase the robustness of the signal to channel attenuations and to increase the coverage area of a terminal. We propose here a cooperative MAC protocol with a low complexity partner selection scheme for packet retransmission. We compare the cooperative and non-cooperative performances through simulations and we show that cooperation allows terminals to maintain the same data rate in an extended coverage area.

articleTitle: Mobile Communication systems and antenna technologies for wireless broadband
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: This presentation first introduces the states of current mobile communication systems in Japan and briefly touches on the states of IMT-Advanced or 4G. Then, the technologies required for base station and terminal antennas in the enhanced mobile communication systems are discussed.

articleTitle: Compact WCDMA and WLAN antenna for mobile equipment
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: A compact, low-profile, planar, microstrip fed, low-cost antenna which can be integrated easily with RF circuitry on the same printed circuit board has been designed for 3G wideband code division multiple access (WCDMA) mobile and WLAN applications.The proposed antenna fills this gap with a small footprint of 18x21 (mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>).The antenna is built on FR-4 type substrate, and the radiating patch is loaded by another FR-4 layer on top.

articleTitle: Characterization of pulse distortion and dispersion of spiral antennas
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: This paper demonstrates that the natural dispersion of spiral antennas can be mitigated by pulse shaping. Specifically, it is shown that the fifth derivative Gaussian pulse with σ = Sips designed for indoor UWB systems can be used to compensate the dispersive properties of the examined spirals. Furthermore, the study shows that the planar equiangular and Archimedean spiral antenna configurations have high and almost constant fidelity factors at different observation angles and at different planes. The study demonstrated a good agreement between the three full-wave modeling methods used in this analysis. It is also shown that as expected the MOM results are more comparable to Friis theoretical transmission formula than the other partial differential equation based methods.

articleTitle: H-shaped dipole array antenna for broadband operation
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: An effective and simple planar dipole antenna has been proposed with a balun transition and the balanced array dipole element. This design methodology is not only simple to implement but also low profile and provides 1.84~2.44 GHz bandwidth with fairly good radiation patterns. Unbalanced currents are compensated for balun transition which provide the equal currents same direction. The dipole generates maximum antenna radiation and efficiency. The present design relates to the planar printed H-shaped array dipole antenna with integrated tapered line balun and suitable for modern wireless applications.

articleTitle: PIFA bandwidth optimization using genetic algorithm and capacitive feeding
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: Genetic Algorithm was used to optimize the ground plane shape of planar inverted F antenna (PIFA) on FR-4 substrate designed for broadband applications. The initial PIFA antenna design had 36% bandwidth and its central frequency was 2 GHz. Novel optimized antennas were presented. A relative bandwidth about 88 % was obtained with the optimized antenna. With this procedure the total bandwidth increased more than 2.5 times relatively the total bandwidth of the not optimized antenna. However, the dimensions and the cost did not increase. This procedure can be very important for the design and optimization of different types of planar antennas to be used in many wireless systems, such as WiFi, WiMax, Bluetooth, etc.

articleTitle: A novel ARQ scheme based on Network Coding Theory in Cognitive Radio networks
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: In this paper, Network Coding (NC) Theory is introduced to improve efficiency of the traditional ARQ scheme for Cognitive Radio (CR) broadcast, named as NC-ARQ, in which we consider making the CR basestation combine the lost packets during ARQ broadcast retransmission in CR networks (CRN), with the changeable availability of CR channel. The Broadcast Cost is defined to indicate and compare the theoretic performance between traditional ARQ scheme and NC-ARQ. Numerical results are analyzed to validate the performance improvement of NC-ARQ.

articleTitle: Improved range resolution for FMCW HF surface wave radar
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: A modified signal processing for FMCW waveform has been proposed that yields an improved range resolution without increasing the transmitted signal bandwidth. The chirp duration is reduced by an appropriate factor while the interval of the beat signal sequence considered for the range transform is kept constant. This modification implies a range transform over several chirp sweeps and an interleaving technique for the Doppler transform. Range resolution is improved without affecting the maximum unambiguous Doppler. This is achieved on the expense of a reduction of the maximum unambiguous range. Actually, this is not a restriction for HF SWR systems where the maximum range is limited by surface wave attenuation. However, a minimum practical range bin size is given either by the size of the targets considered or by the acceptable size of range side lobe level coming along with increasing range resolution. With this approach first and second order sea clutter is reduced which is of significant interest for ship detection.

articleTitle: Identication error analysis of block orthogonal modulations for cognitive radio
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: In this paper, error probability analysis is presented for a block orthogonal modulation identification using General Orthogonal Modulation (GOM). In a N-dimensional space, GOM is defined by a transfer matrix obtained by N-dimensional rotations. The modulation parameters are rotation planes and rotation angles.

articleTitle: Specific Absorption Rate (SAR) safety assessment for Wireless Network after Next (WNaN) radio antennas
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Wireless Information Technology and Systems
abstract: Our primary objective is to provide a safety assessment for the two antennas that are recently developed by the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) under the Wireless Network after Next (WNaN) program.
